lawyer:
Abdul Baset Majumdar with Md Moheshin Miah, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Kazi Shahadat Hossain with Syed Mahmud Hossain, Advocates —For the informant-Petitioner.
parties:
Rashel Kabir alias Roman ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: The informant of Cantonment PS Case No. 84 dated 28-1-1997 (Corresponding GR Case No. 210 of 1997 of the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka) has filed the application for being added as opposite party in the Rule, being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4259 of 1998, which has been obtained by an application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. Petitioner of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case is an accused in the aforementioned case under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. His prayer for bail being without success in the courts below, he moved this court and obtained the Rule calling upon the opposite party the State to show cause as to why he (petitioner) should not be enlarged on bail. At the time of issuance of the Rule, he has been granted ad interim bail. 

 3. Informant-petitioner has filed the application with the prayer for addition of party in the Rule stating, amongst others, that he has obtained all the certified copies of the statements of the witnesses recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and other documents related with this case (GR Case No. 210 of 1997) and, as such, he may be added as opposite party No. 2 in this application (meaning Miscellaneous case) for proper and effective adjudication of the case" and that if he is not added as a party in the Miscellaneous case he shall suffer irreparable loss and injury." 

 4. Learned Advocate Mr Kazi Shahadat Hossain, in support of the prayer for addition of party in the Rule, submits that the petitioner is the informant that is, the person who lodged the First Information Report in the Cantonment PS Case No. 84 dated 28-1-1997 (PS Case No. 84(1) and, as such, when the petitioner (in the Rule) obtained the Rule seeking bail he should have made the informant one of the parties in the said Rule. He further submits that provisions of section 493 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides for appointing a pleader by a private person to assist the public prosecutor and in that state of the matter, petitioner is legally entitled to be added as a party in the Rule. 

 5. Mr Abdul Baset Majumdar, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner (in the Rule), submits that the informant as of right cannot claim to be added as a party in the category of opposite party in the Miscellaneous case in that the same is neither an enquiry nor trial or appeal. He further submits that grounds upon which the informant has prayed for being added as party in the Miscellaneous case do not merit consideration in that, from the four corners of the petition for addition of party if is not seen that he has lost confidence in the prosecutor in charge of the prosecution of the case i.e. Miscellaneous case, and that also there is nothing in the application for addition of party that there is laches of any kind on the part of the prosecutor in charge of the prosecution of the Miscellaneous case. He further submits that the informant has also not expressed any grievance of any kind regarding the prosecutor in charge of the prosecution of the case. 

 6. Mr Munsurul Haque, learned Deputy Attorney-General, has submitted he has nothing to submit in either way as regard the prayer of the informant for being added as opposite party in the Miscellaneous case. He has also submitted that he has appeared upon the impression the Rule, as to which he has instruction to appear, is going to be heard. 

 7. The contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that provisions of section 493 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provide for appointment of pleader in any court by a private person to assist the public prosecutor is correct in respect of enquiry, trial or appeal. The instant proceeding i.e. Miscellaneous case, that has been registered upon an application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is neither an enquiry proceeding nor trial or appeal. In that state of the matter submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner (informant) is legally not eatertainable for being added as opposite party in the Miscellaneous case, and, as such, merits no consideration. 

 8. The other submission is that since the petitioner (informant) lodged an First Information Report and thereupon Cantonment PS case No. 84 dated 28-1-1997 (corresponding GR Case No. 210 of 1997 of the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka) was started and that he being vitally interested in the prosecution of the case petitioner of the Miscellaneous case ought to have made him (informant) a party therein and that having had not done so, prayer for addition of party in the Rule merits consideration. It is seen from the application for addition of party that after completion of investigation police has submitted report for prosecution against 8 persons (including the petitioner in the Miscellaneous case). It is true that petitioner (informant) is interested in the result of the case so started on the basis of his information and that investigated and report to prosecute petitioner and others has been submitted. It is the responsibility of the State to conduct the prosecution through the public prosecutor wherein the petitioner (in the Rule) is an accused. 

 9. Facts stating which petition for addition of party has been filed can hardly be considered as the ground for adding the informant as party in the Miscellaneous case in that the papers, certified copy whereof stated to have been obtained by the petitioner, would much be available to the prosecutor or, in other words, to the Law officer who would represent the State in the Miscellaneous case. Learned Deputy Attorney-General has submitted that he has received instructions to represent the State in the Rule. Furthermore, there is no complaint from the side of the petitioner (informant) that State has lapse or laches in the prosecution of the Miscellaneous case. 

 10. We are of the view that the facts stated and grounds urged in the petition cannot be considered as the ground for being added as the opposite party in the Miscellaneous case.
